transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-01 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Martinez (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Derek Liu (Redwood CSM), Nina Alvarez (Halcyon Head of Security), Samir Patel (CTO), Jorge Ruiz (Infra)

Summary:
Quick security posture discovery for evaluating Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC/on-prem) for Halcyon Health (HIPAA workload). Main concerns: SOC2/ISO status, SSO/SAML and SSO provisioning, RBAC, audit logs retention and accessibility, encryption/KMS/HSM integration, data residency and retention windows, and ability to run in a private VPC or on-prem with customer KMS. End with action items to share certs and schedule deeper perf test.

Topics:
- Compliance: SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, HIPAA/BAA needs
- Identity: SSO (SAML/Okta), SCIM, RBAC and provisioning
- Logs & Auditing: audit logs retention, format, access for forensics
- Encryption & Key Mgmt: KMS, HSM, bring-your-own-key (BYOK)
- Deployment: hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs
- Data retention & residency: purge windows, export, e-discovery

Transcript:
00:00 Alex: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. uh quick intro from our side, im Alex Martinez, AE at Redwood. joined by Priya our solutions engineer and Derek from CSM. you all?
00:07 Nina: hi yes nina here, head of security at Halcyon. thanks for doing this. we've got samir (cto) and jorge (infra) on the call as well.
00:12 Samir: hey all.
00:14 Alex: awesome. goal today is to run through security posture — SOC2, ISO, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, KMS — and map to your reqs, especially since this is PHI and HIPAA territory, right?
00:24 Nina: correct. we need to understand if we can use Redwood hosted or whether we need dedicated or private. our main requirements are strong encryption, control over keys, auditability and a BAA.
00:33 Priya: quick clarifying q: when you say "control over keys" — are you looking for BYOK with HSM-backed KMS or is customer-managed KMS in cloud acceptable?
00:40 Jorge: ideally HSM/BYOK. our security team prefers to have key custody or at least a dedicated KMS tenant. but open to options if the audit trail and controls are strong.
00:50 Alex: got it. to give you a sense — Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and we have ISO 27001; we'll share certs and the pen test summary after the call. for keys we support customer-managed KMS integrations (major clouds) and also private deployments where you can bring your own HSM.
01:05 Nina: will you send the actual reports? SOC2 with scope, and ISO cert, and a recent pen test? we need to kick off our gap analysis.
01:12 Alex: yes we'll send the pack — SOC2 report redacted, ISO cert, penetration test summary and our security whitepaper. i'll drop those by friday.
01:19 Derek: also adding our standard BAA template for review.
01:22 Samir: about identity — we use Okta SAML, SCIM for provisioning. can you confirm SSO SAML + SCIM is supported and how RBAC maps to our groups?
01:30 Priya: yes we have SSO via SAML and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC is role-based and map-able to Okta groups; we expose roles for admin, ops, app-developer, read-only audit, etc. there are some default roles but you can ask for custom roles as part of private/dedicated onboarding.
01:47 Nina: how is admin access controlled? do you have session logs and admin action audit trails? we need to show who did what for compliance.
01:54 Priya: admin actions are logged — we capture user, action, timestamp, ip, request id — and those live in audit logs. for Hosted we retain 90 days by default but can extend retention for enterprise add-ons or via private deployment.
02:07 Nina: 90 days is too short for us; healthcare retention for certain artifacts is 7 years. what are options for long-term retention?
02:14 Alex: two paths — Hosted with extended log retention as an add-on (we can export logs to your cloud storage/S3), or Private/Dedicated where you control the storage and retention directly. We can also provide periodic snapshots for e-discovery.
02:25 Jorge: if we export logs to S3, is the export tamper-evident and do we get md5s or signatures?
02:31 Priya: exports are delivered via secure transfer; you can push logs directly into your bucket using a secured role. we can support signed manifests and we also support streaming audit logs to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) with signed events.
02:43 Samir: on encryption at rest and in transit — what's the model? and can we use our KMS key to encrypt model caches/kv?
02:51 Priya: data in transit is TLS1.2/1.3. at rest we encrypt with AES-256. For KV/cache for inference we support encrypting persisted artifacts and can integrate with customer KMS. For hosted customers we rely on cloud KMS by default but for dedicated/private we also support BYOK and HSM-backed keys. note: some ephemeral caches in memory are not persisted.
03:08 Nina: will Redwood have access to plaintext? we need to know whether keys are accessible to Redwood staff for debugging.
03:15 Alex: generally no — if you use BYOK with private deployment and HSM, Redwood does not have access to your key material. in hosted mode with Redwood-managed KMS, access is tightly controlled and requires internal approvals; we can discuss a least-privilege process in the whitepaper.
03:29 Samir: good. can you describe the private deployment architecture? we prefer VPC peering over internet egress.
03:36 Priya: private deployment runs the control plane in our managed service but the data plane lives in your VPC (or on-prem) depending on the option. we support VPC peering, transit gateway, and in some cases an on-prem appliance. networking configs are in our private deployment checklist.
03:48 Jorge: do you support egress restrictions — i.e., no outbound internet from the inference nodes?
03:52 Priya: yes, we can lock down egress and provide NAT-less configs; updates are pushed via an approved channel. there are tradeoffs for automated upgrades vs strict network isolation — we document them.
04:04 Nina: auditability: we need tamper-evident audit logs, retention for 7 years, and the ability to export logs for legal holds. can that be done in hosted?
04:11 Alex: hosted + enterprise add-on can route logs to your S3/GS bucket or SIEM and we can set up a retention policy. for complete custody and tamper resistance, private/dedicated where you control storage is the stronger option. we can also sign logs with HSM for tamper-evidence if you bring keys.
04:27 Samir: what's the timeline and effort to move from hosted to dedicated/private if we start hosted?
04:33 Alex: typical path is start hosted for quick POC, then move to dedicated reserved capacity or private when you need VPC and BYOK. migration complexity depends on model data and integrations; Priya can outline a migration runbook.
04:42 Priya: migration runbook covers data export, model pinchpoints, KV cache warmup, and DNS changes. we usually see a 3-6 week project for enterprise customers.
04:49 Samir: ok. also curious about regulatory attestations — do you provide SOC2 Type II with HIPAA in scope?
04:56 Alex: SOC2 is Type II; we can provide the report with redactions. for HIPAA we provide a BAA and our controls map to HIPAA requirements. we'll include the mapping doc in the pack.
05:06 Nina: penetration tests — do you do in-house or third-party? we need third-party reports.
05:10 Alex: we engage a third-party for pentests annually; we'll include the summary and remediation timelines.
05:16 Jorge: about RBAC specifics: can we have a read-only "audit" role that cannot modify configs but can view logs and metrics?
05:22 Priya: yes by default we have read-only roles; we can add a specialized audit role that restricts actions and only exposes logging APIs and dashboards.
05:30 Samir: regarding SSO provisioning — how are deprovisions handled? does SCIM immediately revoke tokens and sessions?
05:36 Priya: SCIM deprovisioning removes the user and we invalidate active sessions shortly after — there is a short TTL for sessions that we can shorten in dedicated/private deployments. for hosted there is a standard session revocation window of a few minutes; for stricter needs we recommend private with shorter TTLs or customized session management.
05:56 Nina: what about data retention for model inputs/outputs — do you persist prompts or user data?
06:01 Alex: by default we do not persist customer prompts in training datasets; we do have options for logging inputs/outputs for debugging which are controlled by config and retention policies. for PHI you can disable logging, or route logs to your own storage.
06:13 Samir: any SOC2 control gaps we should be aware of?
06:16 Alex: nothing major; we'll surface the control mapping document. if you have specific reqs (like 7-year retention), that pushes you towards private/dedicated with export, which we can support.
06:26 Derek: i'll follow up with the BAA and our compliance packet.
06:30 Nina: ok thanks. couple of nitty-gritty questions: do you support cert-based mTLS between our clients and the inference nodes?
06:36 Priya: we support TLS mutual auth in private deployments, and mTLS options for dedicated customers with dedicated networking. hosted is standard TLS.
06:44 Jorge: what about log format — do you provide structured JSON logs with fields for request id, user id, model, latency, tokens?
06:50 Priya: yes structured JSON with request_id, user_id (if provided), model, model_version, latency_ms, token_count, node_id. we can include extra fields on request.
06:59 Samir: are audit logs immutable?
07:02 Alex: with hosted we provide append-only logs and can ship signed manifests; with private you can implement immutability policies on your storage.
07:09 Nina: final question: what's the process for security review in procurement — do you have a dedicated security contact?
07:15 Alex: yes you can escalate to our security team; i'll intro you to our security lead in the follow up. typically we provide the security pack, answer questionnaires (SIG/CAIQ), and run a short architecture review with an SE.
07:25 Samir: perfect. next steps then?
07:28 Alex: recap: we will send SOC2 and ISO certs + pen test summary + BAA, Priya will propose dedicated perf test slots and a runbook, and customer will confirm retention/residency specifics.
07:39 Nina: sounds good. thanks everyone.
07:42 Alex: thanks all.

End of call.
